evidence: Current product baseline plus v1.0.0/v1.1.0/v1.2.0 snapshots were compared with 20 pinned repositories; exact file, normalized 16-line, 80-token and AST matches are all zero, with zero manual candidates.
conclusion: No copied-source blocker was identified in the audited corpus.
requiredAction: Retain the corpus lock and rerun on later source changes.

item: Production and non-npm permissive dependency set
evidence: 214 production lock entries use permissive licenses; deterministic THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES covers 201 production packages plus the Minimal and Nord MIT sources, and package gates require project, dependency, Electron and Chromium notices.
conclusion: Compatible in principle with Apache-2.0 under the recorded notice and package controls.
requiredAction: Run notices and package checks for every release candidate.

evidence: 26 development entries require manual copyleft review, including MPL-2.0 lightningcss and LGPL/composite-license sharp-libvips platform packages; none is an application runtime entry.
conclusion: Build-tool and platform package obligations do not extend to Swob source when the packages are not shipped as runtime payload.
requiredAction: Keep development trees out of app.asar and verify every unpacked, ZIP and DMG app.

evidence: One CC-BY-4.0 lock entry is development-only; the runtime allowlist does not package the development tree.
conclusion: No attribution-requiring dataset was identified in the runtime payload.
requiredAction: Keep the package allowlist fail closed; add attribution if future output directly redistributes the dataset.

evidence: AGPL, GPL and Elastic-2.0 repositories are comparison-only at pinned commits; the current scan found no source match.
conclusion: No code from these repositories is used by the audited product baseline.
requiredAction: Do not copy from them; use clean-room work if future remediation ever requires analogous behavior.

evidence: Two comparison repositories lacked sufficient root license evidence at their pinned commits; the current scan found no source match.
conclusion: They remain comparison-only and contribute no product code.
requiredAction: Do not reuse their code without permission.

evidence: Owner-completed rights-chain declaration and IP assignment are retained in a private archive; committed evidence stores only hashes, page counts and signature-block completion.
conclusion: The repository evidence plus private signed records close the pre-1.3.0 ownership gate without publishing personal data.
requiredAction: Retain the private originals under owner control.

evidence: All 64 tracked visual assets are covered by a reviewed hash-bound evidence manifest; unsupported third-party brand icons were removed from runtime and replaced with Swob-owned neutral glyphs.
conclusion: No path-only or unknown-source asset remains cleared by assertion alone.
requiredAction: Run check:asset-evidence and icons:check on every change.

evidence: The public v1.2.0 macOS payload contained 58 unintended worktree files and incomplete outer notices; the current builder uses a runtime allowlist and the shared package verifier rejects private/development paths and missing notices.
conclusion: The historical artifact remains defective, but the identified root cause is now enforced as a release gate.
requiredAction: Do not reuse v1.2.0 artifacts; verify every app copy in the 1.3.0 candidate.

evidence: Local unsigned dual-architecture packaging can prove contents and the exact-six asset contract, but cannot prove Developer ID signing, notarization or Gatekeeper acceptance.
conclusion: PR and merge are allowed only after release-gates and credentialed signing-smoke pass on the exact final SHA; public release additionally requires both modes to pass on merged master.
requiredAction: Compare workflow headSha with the intended commit and stop on any mismatch or verifier failure.

evidence: The current Windows workflow remains an unsigned internal x64 alpha and is not a formal 1.3.0 release artifact.
conclusion: It cannot substitute for the macOS signing evidence and does not block this macOS release candidate.
requiredAction: Keep Windows alpha labeled non-formal until its own signing and release policy exists.
